title: Relay Ground Station–Asia
label: RGS-A
role: RF technical-volume author on capture team; SEIT lead during program execution; Scrum Master
narrative: RGS-A became my first major space-to-ground communications assignment after moving to Boulder. I joined the capture team and authored the RF content of the technical proposal volume before continuing as Systems Engineering, Integration & Test (SEIT) lead. During execution, my biggest challenges were coordinating multiple engineering disciplines and standing up the program's systems engineering processes from scratch. This work supported the development of six relay ground stations on Guam through critical design review. My 2021 University of Chicago Booth Capture Strategy executive program is linked as relevant professional development, without assuming the certificate preceded capture. Two Guam support trips added a more personal side to the experience: an initial site survey with a wrong-turn mountain adventure, followed by a second trip with more colleagues and a successful summit of Mount Lamlam. Most of all, the second Guam visit was about building friendships, trust, and memories with the team.
mediaCredit: Northrop Grumman public RGS-A program imagery; not a personal project photograph

travelStories.title: First Guam trip · the site survey
travelStories.narrative: During the first trip, I tried to climb Guam's highest point, Mount Lamlam, but took the wrong way and reached Mount Jumullong Manglo instead. I lost the trail and had to army-crawl through tall grass to find it before sunset. Cut up from the hike, I drove across the island to a gas station to buy hydrogen peroxide and unexpectedly discovered McKraut's, a packed German restaurant and bar near the beach, where people were enjoying sausages and imported German beer.

title: Re-scalable Aperture for Precision Targeting Radar
label: RAPTR
role: Deputy hardware leadership / CEM & RF management
narrative: After my initial CEM toolkit and SEWIP assignments, RAPTR became my next major radar program in Baltimore. It was developed as a scalable, product-line radar offering targeting the U.S. Army's Future Vertical Lift (FVL) opportunity, alongside drone radar applications. My responsibilities included deputy hardware leadership and RF/CEM engineering management. The product approach sought adaptability across different platform and mission needs; these were target applications, not claims of selection for specific platforms. A separate, publicly documented RAPTR flight demonstration for FVL followed in December 2022, after my Baltimore tenure, and is included solely as program context. The work was recognized by a 2020 Northrop Grumman Good Engineering Award.

title: Internal CEM Toolkit & RF Modeling
label: CEM / RF R&D
role: Algorithm development / computational electromagnetics → hardware engineering management
narrative: One of my first assignments at Northrop Grumman in Baltimore was developing a new computational method for an internal computational electromagnetics (CEM) toolkit, with the goals of handling larger electromagnetic problems and improving execution speed. Separately, I performed CEM analysis supporting SEWIP. Later responsibilities expanded to RF modeling, simulation R&D and engineering management. The work was recognized by a 2020 Northrop Grumman New Technology Award.

title: Resilient Missile Warning & Tracking / Ground Management & Integration
label: RMWT / GMI
role: Capture support → Ground Entry Point (GEP) Lead
narrative: After supporting the RMWT GMI capture effort, I joined the team as Ground Entry Point (GEP) Lead. In contrast to the broad SEIT responsibilities I held on RGS-A, this role focuses specifically on RF systems. I work with inherited GEP sites and help develop an international network. The most memorable experience so far has been a trip to the United Kingdom: staying in Cambridge while working at RAF Molesworth.
